You receive no reference label, optimization feedback or other answers. Code aggregates your observation; do not infer or output the overall label.
Follow the saved question, endpoint, criteria and binding. Compare source and edited evidence when judging a requested change; a source property or an unrelated edited object alone does not establish that the requested change occurred. State the concrete visual feature and region supporting your answer. If evidence is genuinely insufficient use unknown; do not turn uncertainty or failure into No. A clear negative observation can have high confidence. Confidence is not an overall-quality score. program.decomposition_reason: Only one genuinely distinct visual dimension is justified: whether the jacket closure is fully closed. The instruction specifies no separate visual treatment or other change, so a second condition would duplicate the same endpoint or invent a requirement.

d1: The node correctly checks the fully closed endpoint, and its high-confidence fail is supported by the edited image: the jacket hangs open with a conspicuous gap. Do not change the criterion or force the reference label; the reference is an aggregate constraint, not proof that this check should pass. The key issue is rubric alignment: the rubric says “partial” when some requested change has progressed, but this node only emits pass/fail/unknown, and its trace does not assess whether the jacket became more closed than in the source. Add a distinct, evidence-based partial-progress outcome (or route this check’s result into the aggregate progress rubric), comparing the visible closure in source and edit while retaining “pass” only for fully closed and “unknown” for unobservable evidence. Here the source also appears open, and the edit’s panels remain visibly separated; do not infer progress merely from the changed pose or jacket appearance. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated.
